affected_system: public participation, multilingual communication, consultation, and feedback closure
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign
pair randomized encouragement or staggered process evaluation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Invitation, exposure, participation, contribution, response, decision, and trust remain distinct.
Participation records preserve consent, privacy, language, accessibility, and channel provenance.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign.

constraints.description: The public participation and risk communication evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: public engagement director and risk communications lead
decision_question: Did phased language, access, deliberation, or feedback changes improve verified participation and understanding?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The public participation and risk communication evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.decision_object: phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: randomized encouragement or staggered process evaluation
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in verified usable participation and comprehension

intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in verified usable participation and comprehension
distributional gap in change in verified usable participation and comprehension
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer trust, consent, legitimacy, behavior, or policy influence from attendance alone.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased inclusive engagement and communication redesign passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

title: Evaluate inclusive engagement and risk communication
transportability_risks: Trust, language, civic institutions, digital access, deliberation norms, and risk salience differ.
Participants are not automatically representative of affected populations.
